summary: Deep test of live pincode -> India Post location -> 5-source GHI consensus (/api/solar/resource), resilience (monkeypatched unit tests with in-memory fake DB), and calculator Step-1 solar/DISCOM UX plus DISCOM/States/State-detail/Government pages. All 9 requested pincodes resolve to correct state/district with verifiedBy India Post, 5/5 sources, plausible GHI (4.79-5.5) and numeric sunny days (201010 -> 192, no longer '—'). Extra spot checks 396210 Daman, 403722 Goa, 160017 Chandigarh, 605001 Puducherry, 737101 Sikkim, 190001 Srinagar, 500081 Hyderabad, 302001 Jaipur all correct. Validation 422/404 paths correct, no 500s. Fallback chain (partial source failures, outliers, out-of-range, stale cache, geocoder failover, district fallback, state mismatch rejection, all-down -> state_only / 503) verified at unit level. Frontend flows all pass; UI never broke under mocked state_only / 503 / network-abort responses. Found 1 data-trust bug (city not replaced on state switch) and a few minor trust/copy issues.

minor.issue: Zippopotam fallback used (Nominatim/Photon miss) gives 28.6488,77.1726 (central Delhi) for South Delhi PIN 110020 (~14 km off), yet precision is labelled 'pincode' / 'Exact pincode location'. Geocoder results are only state-checked, not district-checked. Impact on GHI is negligible but the label overstates precision.
If a geocoder returns a state string that canon_state() can't map, it is accepted (returns True) instead of being treated as unknown — low risk, but weakens the state-mismatch guard.
period shows plain 'Long-term climatology' — NASA header start/end not present in response, so the years are never displayed.

ui_bugs.issue: State-mismatch 'Switch to Uttar Pradesh' keeps the previously typed City (e.g. 'Jaipur') because patch uses `city: f.city || loc.district`. Result: State=Uttar Pradesh, City=Jaipur, DISCOM=PVVNL — report header shows 'Jaipur, Uttar Pradesh'. When force=true (or when state changes) city should be replaced by loc.district.

Selecting an unverified DISCOM does not overwrite tariff (as designed) but leaves the previous value in the field: after UGVCL->Torrent the field still shows UGVCL's ₹6.9; for Goa it shows the generic default ₹8. User can continue with a number that looks sourced. Consider clearing tariff (forcing entry) or labelling it 'placeholder/previous DISCOM' when the selected DISCOM has ciTariff=null.

issues: Torrent unverified note repeats itself: '...enter the average rate from your bill. Enter the average rate from your bill (total bill ÷ units) in the next step.'
503 error text duplicates the fallback message: 'The calculator will use your state's average. The calculator is using the Uttar Pradesh state average ... meanwhile.'

15 unverified DISCOM cards (Goa, Chandigarh, Puducherry, J&K, Ladakh, DNH, A&N, NE states) have no source link (sourceUrl ''), so [discom-source-link-<id>] is missing for them — 54 links rendered. Add the JERC/SERC URL.

'Solar covers ₹5,79,740' is larger than 'Current bill ₹5,00,000' (BESCOM 560058, ₹5L bill; same for Goa ₹3L -> ₹3,47,561). Net saving math is consistent, but showing solar 'covering' more than the bill is confusing to customers — clarify (e.g. includes exported/escalated value) or cap the displayed figure.

action_items: Fix applyLocation: when force-switching state (weather-switch-state-btn) replace city with loc.district (also consider when f.state was a different state).
For DISCOMs with ciTariff=null, don't silently keep the previous DISCOM's tariff / default 8 — clear the field or mark it clearly as not verified.

Optional: add a district-consistency check (or downgrade precision label) for Zippopotam-only results; add source URLs to unverified DISCOMs; dedupe repeated copy in Torrent note and 503 message; clarify 'Solar covers' > bill in results hero.
critical_code_review_comments: Calculator.jsx is 1086 lines — split Step components / Results into modules.
fetchWeather -> applyLocation reads `f` from the render closure after an await; if the user edits state/city during the fetch, stale values can be written back. Use functional setF.
solar_service: good structure — retries only on 429/5xx, per-source 40s wait_for, geo_cache 90d, solar_cache v3 14d fresh/365d stale, never-500 catch in server.py. Confirmed via unit tests.
get_solar does not cache results with sourcesUsed<2 (returned live with low confidence) — fine, but repeated calls for such spots will re-hit all 5 APIs every time.

context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini forces xdist (-n 2); for serial use `-n 0` not `-p no:xdist`. Unit tests in test_solar_service_unit.py monkeypatch solar_service.SOURCES/_india_post/_nominatim_pin/etc. with a FakeDB (no Mongo). Toggle testids: weather-toggle-true / weather-toggle-false. Step tabs: step-tab-1..4. Live Estimate panel has no data-testids (read via text 'Live Estimate'). UI fallback states verified by page.route mocking of /api/solar/resource.
rca of the issue: City mismatch: Calculator.jsx applyLocation builds patch `{ state: loc.state, city: f.city || loc.district }`, so an existing city from a different state survives the forced state switch. Repro: /calculator -> State Maharashtra, City Jaipur (or any) -> pincode 201010 -> Get live solar data -> Switch to Uttar Pradesh -> City remains 'Jaipur'. Mitigation: `city: (force || f.state !== loc.state || !f.city) ? (loc.district || f.city) : f.city`.
